beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered. Greeting: Shalom, Liam (Hebrew hello).
beats.narration_text: Shalom, Liam. One Claude prompt. An animated MTAP passenger deletion — chromosome bar, two genes lost in one cut, and the metabolic dependency that makes the accident actionable.

props.command: claude "Port the mtap-passenger plate from plates_gen.py p13() into Manim. Chromosome bar (GRAY) with 5 ticks, 2 deleted (driver BLUE square + passenger ORANGE circle, pulled below). Passenger circle arrows down to SKY accumulation node with 5 dots. VERM plug from right blocks node. Animate: bar, deletion, flow to node, plug blocks."

beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — what passenger deletion IS
beats.narration_text: Chromosomal deletions don't always remove just the target gene. When a driver gene is cut, neighboring genes get deleted too — passengers. MTAP sits next to CDKN2A, one of the most frequently deleted tumor suppressors. Lose CDKN2A, and MTAP goes with it in roughly half of all human cancers.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — chromosome diagram with CDKN2A (driver, BLUE) and MTAP (passenger, ORANGE) as adjacent genes; deletion bracket over both; '~50% of human cancers' label

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — what MTAP loss creates therapeutically
beats.narration_text: MTAP loss creates a metabolic dependency. Without MTAP, a metabolite accumulates and cells become hyperdependent on PRMT5. Inhibit PRMT5 — an enzyme tumor cells need, normal cells don't — and MTAP-deleted cells die. The deletion that was an accident becomes the vulnerability.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — metabolite accumulation arrow; PRMT5 enzyme box highlighted; 'accident → vulnerability' text; split panel tumor vs normal cell

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the MTAP passenger plate from plates underscore gen dot py — p thirteen — into a Manim scene. Chromosome bar in gray spanning the full width. Five tick marks, with the second and third removed. A vermillion bracket arc above the deleted segment. Below the bar: a blue square for the driver gene and an orange circle for the passenger, pulled downward. From the orange passenger circle: an arrow down to a sky-blue accumulation node with five dots inside. A vermillion plug triangle from the right, arrow pointing at the node. Animate in order: bar and ticks, bracket, deletion with the two shapes falling below, the arrow growing to the accumulation node, the dots appearing, the plug arriving.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_MtapPassenger class, trimmed to what teaches. sparkLine ≤ 4 words.
beats.narration_text: Read it. The chromosome bar is a RoundedRectangle spanning negative six to positive six — a single shape, no loop needed. The tick marks are three Line objects; the second and third positions are skipped by index. The driver square and passenger circle start at bar level and animate downward — that falling motion is a VGroup animate to a new y-value. The accumulation node is a Circle with five dot children added as a VGroup, each FadeIn with a tiny lag. The plug is a Triangle pointing left, arriving on a GrowFromEdge. The whole thing reads left to right, then top to bottom: deletion, consequence, block.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_MtapPassenger
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
config.background_color = "#FFFFFF"
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; ORANGE="#E69F00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_MtapPassenger(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    bar = RoundedRectangle(width=12,height=0.45,
      corner_radius=0.1,color=GRAY,
      fill_color=GRAY,fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([0,2.5,0])
    tick_xs=[-4.8,-2.4,0,2.4,4.8]
    ticks=VGroup(*[Line([x,2.73,0],[x,2.27,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=3)
      for i,x in enumerate(tick_xs) if i not in [1,2]])
    driver=Square(side_length=0.7,color=BLUE,
      fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.2).move_to([-0.8,2.5,0])
    passenger=Circle(radius=0.4,color=ORANGE,
      fill_color=ORANGE,fill_opacity=0.2).move_to([0.8,2.5,0])
    # animate deletion — shapes fall below bar
    self.play(Create(bar),Create(ticks))
    bracket=ArcBetweenPoints([-2.4,2.95,0],[2.4,2.95,0],
      angle=-PI/3,color=VERM,stroke_width=3)
    self.play(Create(bracket))
    self.play(FadeIn(driver),FadeIn(passenger))
    self.play(driver.animate.move_to([-0.8,1.0,0]),
      passenger.animate.move_to([0.8,1.0,0]))

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_MtapPassenger — watch the deletion fall and accumulation node build
beats.narration_text: Run it. The chromosome bar appears, then the three surviving tick marks. The vermillion bracket materialises above the gap — marking exactly what was deleted. The driver and passenger shapes fade in at bar level and then fall below it — that downward motion is the deletion made spatial. The arrow grows from the passenger circle to the accumulation node, then the five sky-blue dots appear one by one. The plug arrives from the right and points at the node. The diagram now reads: passenger lost, metabolite builds, exit blocked.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: after the deletion, make the orange passenger circle pulse with a Flash to show it is the vulnerable node. Then animate the five dots flowing one at a time downward into the accumulation node — each dot moves from its source position into the node centre on a LaggedStart. Then move the plug along its arrow path toward the node, and fire a sky-blue Flash on the node as the plug arrives. The viewer needs to see accumulation in motion, then the block.

claude "Revise: after deletion, ORANGE passenger pulses (Flash). Dots flow
one-at-a-time downward into accumulation node (animate position, LaggedStart).
VERM plug moves along arrow to node (animate position). Flash on node as blocked."

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with causal flow
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_MtapPassengerFlow — deletion + passenger pulse + dot flow + plug arrival
beats.narration_text: Watch the flow now. Same deletion sequence as before — bar, bracket, shapes fall. Then the passenger pulses orange: this is the gene that accumulates the metabolite. Five dots lift off and flow one by one into the accumulation node — each one a unit of metabolite building up because MTAP is gone. Then the plug moves along its arrow path toward the node, and when it arrives the node flashes sky-blue. The circuit is: deletion causes accumulation causes dependency. Now you can see it move.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: The passenger opened the door. Chromosome deletion — passenger lost — metabolite accumulates — drugable dependency created. A therapeutic target born from collateral damage.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — four-step causal chain: Chromosome deletion → passenger lost → metabolite accumulates → drugable dependency; 'collateral damage → therapeutic target' tagline

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: given the MTAP deletion, write a Manim scene showing the PRMT5 dependency — accumulating metabolite dots flowing toward a PRMT5 enzyme shape that consumes them and produces a cell-survival signal; then a second panel where PRMT5 is blocked and dots overflow, cell death follows. Why run it? Because this extension shows the therapeutic mechanism, not just the vulnerability. The first scene shows what goes wrong. The PRMT5 scene shows why the wrong thing is exploitable — the accumulation that kills normal pathway function is exactly the handle the inhibitor grabs. Animate the mechanism and you animate the drug logic.
